memories.content: The user used an accessible entrance at a clinic in December 2024.
On a day snow had accumulated and blocked the main-entrance ramp, the user went to a side entrance.
The user learned on site that the elevator was under inspection and delayed the appointment.
The day before the next visit, the user called to check whether the elevator would be operating.
The user waited for their turn in front of a ticket machine near the waiting chairs.
On a day the user waited in a corridor without chairs, they leaned against the wall and changed position several times.
On a day their older sister accompanied them, the user found a place to sit immediately after reception.
Reception staff expect that a first-time visitor may ask where the accessible entrance is.
The local agent cannot infer the user's condition from a record of using an accessible route alone.
Snow accumulation and snow-removal work can temporarily block an entrance route used under ordinary conditions.
The user reviewed their emergency-contact list in February 2025.
When preparation instructions arrived as a long paragraph, the user missed two items.
After changing the same content into a checklist, the user marked every item they had prepared.
The user called their mother on a weekend evening, but they spoke only briefly because the mother was out.
The user called again on Saturday morning the following week and spoke for 40 minutes.
The user sent a text to an old number for an emergency contact and saw that delivery failed.
After confirming the new number with their older sister, the user updated the contact list.
For nonurgent contact, the user's older sister prefers to reply by text when available rather than take a call immediately.
Before using an emergency contact, reconfirm the number and relationship information with the user.
The user feels that a reminder the day before an appointment gives them enough time to recheck preparation items.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains without materially overlapping claims: the reference records clinic access, mobility, waiting, and inference limits, while the compared frame records preparation formats, family contact patterns, emergency-contact maintenance, and reminder timing. No contradiction or scope-based cross-frame difference is established.
